Not a difference: the reference uses task.finished_speed or task.speed, but finished_speed is only set when total is known (base/rich/progress.py finish block, guarded by 'task.total is not None'), so for total-None tasks the generated task.speed gives the same value.
Regression check: for total-known tasks or show_speed=False the else branch (generated/rich/progress.py:715-716) matches base lines 704-706, so existing behavior is unchanged.
criteria.deficiency: The patch implements only the column-level option. The track()-level option that defines the feature is missing, and the unknown-total path through track() still raises ValueError. Even at the column level, the speed display differs from the reference in number format (no unit scaling, always two decimals) and in style (unstyled by default).
